It is a snapshot of the website with minor modifications as it appeared on August 26, 2015.' No separate archive snapshot verified.
note: A state historic preservation office's field guide: later scholarship, written to help people identify a building's style from its features, which is exactly what the style library's 'how to spot it' cues are. It is a Pennsylvania guide, so it describes the national styles as they appear there; every cue taken from it is a general feature of the style, never a claim about a Chicago building. The Commercial style page says the style 'is sometimes referred to as the Chicago style' and describes the 'Chicago window'.
what_it_supplies: the identifying features of the Greek Revival, Italianate, Second Empire, Queen Anne and Commercial (Chicago) styles

what_it_does_not_supply: the style of any particular Chicago building
